findings.claim: The fix only changes isPlatformRole in packages/shared, but the ticket explicitly names requireKeyAdmin's own toUpperCase in services/security/src/index.ts as a second admission point; that path is untouched, so the dotless-i/long-s/array spellings may still be admitted there.
findings.evidence: keyRevokePolicy.ts:140-144 `export function isPlatformRole(role: string | undefined): boolean { ... if (typeof role !== 'string') return false; return PLATFORM_ROLES.has(role.replace(/[a-z]/g, (ch) => ch.toUpperCase())); }`; ticket: "services/security/src/index.ts — requireKeyAdmin's toUpperCase"
findings.test_or_reason: The diff touches only keyRevokePolicy.ts and the new test file; no change to services/security/src/index.ts, and no test covers requireKeyAdmin. The ticket's own 'Where' section lists it as a second location to fix.

findings.claim: The ticket's acceptance criterion 'reject a non-string role outright, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it' is not met because the shared definition is not the only definition; requireKeyAdmin still has its own toUpperCase comparison that is not fixed.
findings.evidence: Ticket: "Compare against an exact ASCII-folded string and reject a non-string role outright, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it." and "services/security/src/index.ts — requireKeyAdmin's toUpperCase"
findings.test_or_reason: The diff only modifies isPlatformRole; requireKeyAdmin is not touched, so the 'one shared definition' goal is not achieved.

findings.claim: The new test file's claim that 'every spelling the platform really uses is still admitted' is not fully pinned: the test only checks SUPER_ADMIN/SYSTEM_ADMIN in a few casings, but does not test the exact set of role strings that the platform actually issues (e.g., from auth service), so the control is incomplete.
findings.evidence: test file lines 37-50: C1-C3 test only 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'super_admin', 'system_admin', 'Super_Admin', 'sYsTeM_aDmIn'
findings.test_or_reason: The comment in the test header says 'every spelling the platform really uses is still admitted', but the test does not enumerate the platform's actual role vocabulary; it only tests a few variants.

findings.claim: The fix's ASCII fold via regex replace is functionally equivalent to toUpperCase for ASCII letters, but the comment says 'every other character untouched' — this is true for the regex, but the code does not explicitly reject non-ASCII characters that are not in the regex; they pass through unchanged and could still match if the set contained them (it doesn't, but the comment's claim of 'exact ASCII fold' is slightly overstated).
findings.evidence: keyRevokePolicy.ts:144 `return PLATFORM_ROLES.has(role.replace(/[a-z]/g, (ch) => ch.toUpperCase()));` and comment line 142 "Only an ASCII fold is applied (a-z to A-Z, every other character untouched)"
findings.test_or_reason: The regex only replaces a-z; any other character (including non-ASCII) is left as-is, so the fold is not a full ASCII fold (e.g., it does not fold other Unicode case pairs), but since the set only contains ASCII uppercase, it is safe. The comment's wording is slightly imprecise.

findings.claim: The ticket's 'Reachability is NOT established' caveat is not addressed by the PR; the fix is a hardening measure but does not prove that any issuer can actually sign a dotless-i role, so the severity remains a nit per the ticket's own framing.
findings.evidence: Ticket: "Reachability is NOT established, and that is the first thing to settle ... The gate did not test whether any issuer, user-management path or seed can store or sign one, and nor have I. So the severity here is a nit until someone measures that"
findings.test_or_reason: The PR does not add any test or measurement of reachability; it only changes the predicate.
